conclusion.next_question: If the architecture were federated, where should the model boundaries sit?
paragraphs: The evidence does not support treating the 815 active pathways as independent units. Most sit within one connected structure,there are 3,478 distinct pathway-to-pathway links, and about 63% of referenced questions are reused across more than one pathway.

Pathway size also varies materially: the typical pathway contains 25 questions while the largest contains 174. Existing classifications such as Symptom Groups, Clinical Areas, age and trauma provide useful structure, but overlap and do not bythemselves create clean computational boundaries.

Phase 1 therefore provides a reliable structural basis for the next question: whethercoherent candidate Bayesian families can be derived from this connected estate. It doesnot determine whether a federated architecture is preferable.
conclusion.title: NHS Pathways is a connected, shared clinical decision estate

cards.explanation: Individual transfer instructions in the data. Several can create the same link.
cards.label: Recorded handover instructions

cards.explanation: The largest set of pathways reachable from one another by following handovers in any direction.
cards.label: Pathways in the largest connected group

cards.explanation: Pathways that neither hand over nor receive handovers.
cards.label: Pathways with no handovers

connectivity.definition: A link exists between two pathways when an answer in the first can hand the assessment over to the second. Links are counted once per pair and direction, however many answers create them.
connectivity.presentation_note: The full network is not drawn. At this size a single node-link diagram is unreadable and would not support any conclusion. The distributions and the family-level view in Phase 2 carry the same information legibly.

does_not_tell_us: Whether one large Bayesian Network or several smaller ones is the better design — in technical terms, monolithic against federated. Phase 1 measures the estate; it does not compare architectures.
Which Bayesian families should exist. Phase 2 proposes candidates; none is confirmed.
How large a Bayesian model built from this data would be, in nodes, edges or probability tables.
How much memory or compute a model would need, or how fast it would answer.
What infrastructure would be required, or what it would cost to run, including any cloud infrastructure cost.
How often each pathway is actually used. The dataset carries structure, not traffic, so a rarely-used pathway counts the same as a busy one.

cards.explanation: A pathway is one clinical assessment flow, such as the assessment for a particular symptom. Active means in use rather than archived.
cards.label: Active pathways

cards.explanation: Distinct questions available to ask across the whole estate. Many are used by more than one pathway.
cards.label: Questions

cards.explanation: The possible responses to those questions. Each answer can lead somewhere different.
cards.label: Answers

cards.explanation: Each row records what happens after a specific answer to a specific question in a specific pathway. This is the wiring of the whole estate.
cards.label: Triage logic relationships

cards.explanation: The possible outcomes of an assessment, such as an ambulance response or a primary-care referral within a stated time.
cards.label: Dispositions

cards.explanation: An existing NHS classification that groups pathways by presenting symptom.
cards.label: Symptom groups

cards.explanation: Clinical factors that distinguish more urgent presentations from less urgent ones.
cards.label: Symptom discriminators

cards.explanation: A broad anatomical or clinical grouping, such as chest or head. A pathway can belong to more than one.
cards.label: Clinical areas

cards.explanation: Distinct ways one pathway can hand over to another. Derived by resolving every recorded transfer instruction to its target pathway.
cards.label: Pathway-to-pathway links

executive_summary.bottom_line: Phase 1 supports proceeding to family discovery. It does not decide whether the finalBayesian architecture should be monolithic or federated.
executive_summary.headline: NHS Pathways is one connected clinical decision estate, not hundreds of isolated pathways.
key_points: 767 active pathways sit in the largest connected group, with 3,478 distinct pathway-to-pathway relationships.
About 63% of referenced questions are reused across more than one pathway, so the estate contains substantial shared clinical structure.
Pathway size varies materially: the typical pathway contains 25 questions while the largest contains 174.
Existing classifications such as Symptom Groups, Clinical Areas, age and traumaprovide useful signals, but overlap and do not cleanly divide the estate.
executive_summary.summary: Phase 1 examined the structure of 815 active pathways and found extensive connectivity, reuse and variation in size. The evidence is strong enough to move fromdescribing the estate to testing where meaningful Bayesian family boundaries might sit.

groupings.caveat: These are existing NHS classifications and possible grouping signals. None of them is automatically a Bayesian family: Phase 2 tests how well each one actually holds together.

clinical_area_overlap.note: A pathway can be listed under several clinical areas, so the area counts add up to more than the number of pathways. Clinical areas overlap; they are not a clean division of the estate.

meta.confidentiality: Contains derived NHS Pathways analysis. Handle according to programme information governance requirements.

evidence_classes.candidate: A possible grouping, boundary or shared structure suggested by the evidence. Requires clinical review and architectural judgement before it means anything.
evidence_classes.derived: Calculated from measured values using a stated definition. The definition is given with the figure.
evidence_classes.measured: Counted directly in the NHS Pathways dataset.

meta.question: What does NHS Pathways actually look like?
meta.scope_note: This report presents measured and derived evidence only. It makes no architectural recommendation: comparing monolithic against federated designs is Phase 3 work.
meta.title: Understanding NHS Pathways

methodology.definition: A pathway, question or disposition not archived and not flagged for deletion. Applied only to the tables that record both flags.

Distinct answerable triage questions referenced by a pathway's logic. The same column in the source data also references care-advice and disposition steps; those are counted separately, because only answerable questions could become variables in a model.
A transfer instruction of the form <pathway>.<step> whose pathway part matches a real pathway, aggregated to one link per source, target and direction.
One transfer value in the source data. A single answer can carry up to four, one per skillset branch, so instructions outnumber links.
A set of pathways reachable from one another by following handovers in either direction. Formally a weakly connected component.
For a group of pathways: handovers that stay inside the group as a share of all handovers leaving the group's pathways. 100% means the group is self-contained.

Navigation codes that carry no destination in the data are treated as control behaviour, not handovers. If any of them does imply a relationship recorded elsewhere, the connectivity figures understate it.

pathway_size.definition: Questions counted per pathway are the answerable triage questions only. Care-advice and disposition steps are counted separately and excluded here.

reuse.definition: A question is counted as reused when more than one pathway references it. Reuse is counted from the recorded wiring, not from how often a question is actually asked.

tells_us.text: There are 3,478 distinct ways one pathway can hand over to another, and 767 of the 815 active pathways sit in a single connected group. Any design has to account for that.
tells_us.title: The estate is connected, not a set of independent pathways

tells_us.text: The typical pathway asks 25 questions, but the largest asks 174. A design sized for the typical case would not fit the largest.
tells_us.title: Pathways vary widely in size

tells_us.text: About 63% of the questions referenced by triage logic are used by more than one pathway. The same clinical question appears in many places.
tells_us.title: Most question content is shared between pathways

tells_us.text: 22 clinical areas and 365 symptom groups are already recorded, alongside age and trauma tags. A pathway can belong to several at once, so none of them divides the estate cleanly.
tells_us.title: Several grouping systems already exist, and they overlap

tells_us.text: Every recorded handover instruction resolved to a real target except four, and all internal navigation steps resolved. Known gaps are reported rather than filled in.
tells_us.title: The data is good enough to build evidence on
